use.reason: The displayed two matrix products in the consumer give the dilation and normalized U_p² action. For c nonzero divisible by4, the character d -> (c/d) has conductor dividing |c|: write c=s²D with D the fundamental discriminant of its squareclass; the factor at2 is at most the 2-part of c. This includes c negative. Hence d-prime congruent d modulo c preserves that character, and d-prime congruent d modulo4 preserves epsilon. Since p does not divide d-prime, (p²/d-prime)=1. For V_p, multiplicativity gives (c/p /d)/(c/d)=(p/d). All square-root arguments are identically cz+d, so there is no branch comparison by squaring. If c=0, d=±1 and the same matrices give the triangular identity directly. The map r->(b+rd)/(a+rc) modulo p² is a bijection since a+rc is a unit and determinant is1. A finite set of rational translates has rational cusp images; after choosing a common cusp width, each expansion has nonnegative exponents, so the finite sum is holomorphic. Finally U_p² V_p=U_p coefficientwise. At each new p, p is prime to all previously fixed level factors, and this argument does not raise their exponents.

use.reason: For a unary generator F_lambda(tz), psi=lambda*chi_-4*(t/.). Choose a good p outside t and the character/sieve modulus. At n=t m² the first term is p lambda(p)a(n). If p does not divide m, the middle term is lambda(p)a(n), because chi_-4(p)*(t/p)*(-t/p)=1, and the last term is zero. If p divides m, the middle term is zero and the last term is lambda(p)a(n), including zero coefficients of the imprimitive character. At indices outside t times a square all three terms vanish. Thus the eigenvalue is lambda(p)(p+1), of absolute value p+1. The standard unary space is spanned by such generators: a one-variable lattice/coset theta has a periodic odd coefficient after clearing denominators; partition its finite residue set by gcd strata and expand each function on the remaining unit group in Dirichlet characters. Oddness retains only odd characters, and a gcd factor becomes a square dilation. For any fixed finite collection these presentations have a common finite bad set. Only one prime outside it is needed below.

use.reason: Let U be the unary subspace of the fixed finite-dimensional cusp space and W=U-perp. The preceding coefficient calculation gives T(U) subset U; the exact published statement gives T(W) subset W. Therefore the orthogonal decomposition is T-block-diagonal and also T-adjoint-block-diagonal, without choosing a potentially different normalization for an adjoint formula. If f is in the actual elliptic eigenspace, its U projection is an eigenvector of T with the same eigenvalue eta(p)a_p(E). Choose a prime outside the finite bad set of a unary spanning set, the actual level and E. All eigenvalues of T restricted to U have absolute value p+1, whereas the separately retained Hasse input gives absolute value at most2sqrt(p)<p+1. The U projection is zero. Thus f lies in W and both spaces are stable under the relevant good operators and their adjoints.
